To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CFS composite beams with tubular flange packed with lightweight packing material are more efficient compared to the CFS composite beam with flat flanges and also compared to the CFC beams.
CFS composite beams are more ductile than CFS beams and the ultimate strength of CFS composite beams is more than CFS beams.
CFS composite beams are a viable alternative to traditional steel beams and that the use of packing materials in CFS beams improves their load carrying capacities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel light weight CCF composite beam with rectangular box section.
developing a new generation of lightweight CFS beams for use in the construction industry, which are more economical, efficient and environmentally sustainable.
the development of novel lightweight cold formed steel (LFCS) composite beams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CFS composite beams packed with lightweight packing materials are very promising and can be used in the design of light weight structural systems.
the novel CFS composite beam sections are more efficient than the conventional CFS beams.
the novel light weight CFC beams with rectangular cross section have exhibited better flexural performance compared to their conventional counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CFS composite beams with rectangular box sections, packed with suitable packing material, are more efficient and economical compared to their conventional counterparts.
these beams are very suitable to be used as structural components in the construction of light weight structures like bridges and buildings.
, the novel CFS composite beam with concrete packing has shown the highest flexural strength and ductility among the tested specimens.

these beams can be used in a variety of structural and non-structural applications, such as, in residential, industrial and commercial buildings, as well as, in bridges and other infrastructural applications.

the use of suitable packing materials in cold formed steel beams can improve the flexural performance considerably, thus providing an opportunity to use them in the construction of lightweight, low cost and sustainable structures in future.
